sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: regulatory, railroad, work zone and guide signs
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical guide page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The speed limit page states one maximum for interstates in its paragraph and a different value for rural interstates and freeways in its table, so neither interstate maximum is taught until the conflict is resolved [A02] (verify MO-SIGN-D-INTERSTATEMAX).
The other table rows for rural expressways, urbanized freeways, other non-urban roads and lettered roads were taught as printed, and are isolated as dynamic [A02].
The railroad and work zone pages show sign pictures and typical setup diagrams with no extractable layout detail; only written meanings were used [A03].
The work zone fine paragraph cites its statute; the amounts were restated in original words [A03].
Route sign shapes are pictured, not described in text, so no shape was assigned to a road type [A06].

corpus_stability.reason: The Missouri Driver Guide prints a single edition line on its front cover (Revised August 2026); its table-of-contents note says law and policy changes may make parts out of date and points to the website for the current version, with no sign in the selected pages of more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 52 says in its paragraph that the maximum speed limit on Missouri interstates is one value, while the roadway maximum speed table on the same page lists a higher value for rural interstates and freeways; the current statutory maximum must be confirmed from an official Missouri source before any interstate maximum is taught.
